summary: H.R. 1834 extends certain enhanced premium tax credits and income eligibility rules under the Internal Revenue Code through the end of 2028.

affected_groups.effect: They may continue to receive increased premium assistance amounts and maintain credit eligibility even if household income exceeds 400 percent of the poverty line through taxable years ending before January 1, 2029.
affected_groups.group: Taxpayers and individuals receiving premium tax credits

key_provisions: Extends rules that increase premium assistance amounts from through 2025 to through 2028.
Extends the expiration date for these increased assistance rules from before January 1, 2026, to before January 1, 2029.
Extends the rule allowing the tax credit to taxpayers whose household income exceeds 400 percent of the poverty line from through 2025 to through 2028.
Extends the expiration date for allowing the credit above 400 percent of the poverty line from before January 1, 2026, to before January 1, 2029.
Applies these amendments to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
missing_information: The source text does not specify the exact financial cost of the extensions.
The source text does not state the exact number of people who will be affected.
The source text does not detail the specific dollar amounts of the tax credits.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 1834 extends certain enhanced premium tax credits and income eligibility rules under the Internal Revenue Code through the end of 2028.
summary_detail.significance: The bill extends tax credit policies for three additional years, affecting individuals relying on premium assistance for health coverage.
